```cpp
template <typename Context, typename... Args>

```

And `arg_data`:
```cpp
template <typename T, typename Char, size_t NUM_ARGS, size_t NUM_NAMED_ARGS>
struct arg_data {
  T args_[1 + (NUM_ARGS != 0 ? NUM_ARGS : 1)];
  named_arg_info<Char> named_args_[NUM_NAMED_ARGS];
  ...
};

template <typename T, typename Char, size_t NUM_ARGS>
struct arg_data<T, Char, NUM_ARGS, 0> {
  T args_[NUM_ARGS != 0 ? NUM_ARGS : 1];
  ...
};
```

The `arg_data` specialization is chosen based on `NUM_NAMED_ARGS` (the template parameter). And `num_named_args` is computed from the args. These should be consistent.

```cpp
format_arg get(int id) const {
    format_arg arg = do_get(id);
    if (arg.type_ == internal::type::named_arg_type)
```

`deserialize`:
```cpp
template <typename Context> basic_format_arg<Context> deserialize() const {
    basic_format_arg<Context> arg;
    std::memcpy(&arg, data, sizeof(basic_format_arg<Context>));
    return arg;
}
```

`data` is `char data[sizeof(basic_format_arg<buffer_context<Char>>)]`. If `sizeof(basic_format_arg<Context>)` > `sizeof(basic_format_arg<buffer_context<Char>>)`, then `memcpy` reads past `data`. 

But in the fuzzer, `Context` is `format_context` (char) and `buffer_context<Char>` is `buffer_context<char>` = `basic_format_context<back_insert_iterator<buffer<char>>, char>`. Are these the same size? Let me check.

Actually, `basic_format_arg<Context>` contains `value<Context>` and `type`. `value<Context>` is a union. The largest member is 16 bytes (int128/uint128/long_double). So `sizeof(basic_format_arg<Context>)` is 24 bytes regardless of Context (as long as the union is dominated by 16-byte members). So `deserialize` copies 24 bytes from a 24-byte `data` array. No over-read.
